title: U.S. House · Oregon's 3rd District
area: Most of Multnomah County (inner and east Portland), northeastern Clackamas County, and all of Hood River County.

context.text: Incumbent Maxine Dexter defeated Jessica Salas and Andrew Castilleja with 89.1% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. Loran Ayles ran unopposed for the Republican nomination.

summary.text: Maxine Dexter is the Democratic nominee for re-election to Oregon's 3rd Congressional District, which she has represented since 2025. She is a physician and former chair of the Oregon House Housing and Homelessness Committee.

background.text: Born in Seattle, Washington, in 1972; earned a bachelor's degree in political science and communications and an M.D. from the University of Washington.

Practiced for over 15 years as a lung and critical-care physician at Kaiser Permanente, where she was elected chair of the Board of Directors at Northwest Permanente, the first woman to hold the role.

Appointed to the Oregon House of Representatives in 2020 for the 33rd District, where she chaired the House Housing and Homelessness Committee and led passage of a multi-billion-dollar bill addressing housing and homelessness; also worked on abortion access, addiction treatment, public lands and gun-violence legislation before being elected to Congress in 2024.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Subcommittee on Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs; Subcommittee on Health) and is Ranking Member of the Natural Resources Committee's Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.

As an Oregon state representative, chaired the House Housing and Homelessness Committee and sponsored legislation to address the state's housing and homelessness crisis, addiction treatment, abortion access, and gun violence.
